name: Every top-up run records the date each pair's frozen history actually reaches
notes: Repointed goal-desk-iter-34 by developer (assigned in the iteration's Golden replay script maintenance section). The PRIOR version of this script pinned the exact values of the topup-2026-07-31-8fb5c9a1f737 run AS COMPUTED BY THE BUG this iteration fixes: step 2 asserted the literal text 'newest recorded reach 2026-07-30 . 101 pairs reach it' and step 4 asserted 'AAPL 4h -- 2026-07-30' as an EARLIER row -- i.e. the golden script enshrined the exact contradiction (`topupLibraryReach` grouped the newest-reach extreme and the earlier partition by comparing the full microsecond-precision `store_frozen_through_after` string, while the render printed only the calendar day) that iter-34 corrects. After the day-precision fix, the SAME ambient run's own 404 outcomes re-group as: 303 pairs share the newest calendar day (2026-07-30) and 101 pairs are genuinely earlier (all recorded 2026-07-27) -- the exact inverse of what the buggy 101/303 split showed. This script therefore no longer pins ANY specific date, count, or symbol -- every step below asserts a STABLE structural substring or a testid's mere presence, so it survives both the fix itself and every future real ambient top-up run (the J-09/J-17/J-18 hardening precedent).

This replay script is DELIBERATELY READ-ONLY (goto + expect only, no click) so it never triggers a new top-up run -- the shipped Top-up button walks a real ~100-symbol universe against the live Yahoo adapter, which this era's own NOTES/anti-goals reserve for an explicit, separately-reported operator act, never an automated regression lane (the same J-09/J-17/J-18 precedent).

Step 2 asserts the stable tail '... reach it' every reach line renders regardless of the actual date/count. Step 3 asserts the stable heading substring 'Pairs recorded earlier' (the parenthesized true-total count is not part of the asserted substring, so it drifts freely). Step 4 asserts only that at least one `desk-topup-run-latest-reach-earlier-row` element renders (existence, no text pinned) -- proving the earlier list has genuine row-level markup without asserting any row's own symbol/timeframe/date, which is exactly the content the OLD step 4 wrongly enshrined as correct.

Step 5 asserts only that the new `desk-topup-run-latest-reach-earlier-cap` disclosure element renders (existence, no text pinned) -- true against the CURRENT ambient run because its true earlier-pairs total (101) exceeds the 20-row display cap this iteration adds. This is an honestly environment-dependent assertion, the same class J-09.json's/J-17.json's/J-18.json's own notes document for their asserted run stats: if a future real ambient top-up run ever reduces the true earlier-total to 20 or fewer (e.g. because most pairs converge onto one recent day), this step will need removing or updating -- an honest environmental change, not a product regression.

Step 6 is a post-match liveness re-check (the J-09/J-17/J-18 precedent): a further /desk navigation after the key assertions, proving the page is still alive and rendering correctly, not merely that the earlier matches happened a moment before a crash.
